item.title: TransLink announces service changes for FIFA World Cup in Vancouver
item.description: TransLink is increasing its service in preparation for Vancouver hosting seven FIFA World Cup matches this summer.

item.title: Suspect in Vancouver Starbucks stabbing in 2023 testifies at his murder trial
item.description: A man accused of murder in a fatal stabbing at a Vancouver Starbucks has been called to testify at his trial after his defence lawyer argued he was suffering from a mental illness on the day of the killing.

item.title: VGH to divert pregnant trauma patients amid OB/GYN shortage
item.description: The biggest hospital in the province is about to be the latest forced to divert patients due to a shortage of OBGYNs.

item.title: Vancouver mayor apologizes for comments accusing rival councillor of handing out illegal drugs
item.description: Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim has publicly apologized after he alleged that an opposition city councillor publicly handed out illegal drugs.

item.title: B.C.’s move to end clock changes won’t be without complications
item.description: The mayor of Prince George in northern British Columbia is the father of six adult children, who got used to the struggle of getting his kids out of bed on dark winter mornings as they were growing up.

item.title: Carney won’t say whether India is engaged in interference, transnational repression
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney is refusing to say whether he believes India is still behind acts of foreign interference and transnational repression in Canada.

item.title: Vancouver burglars use hot glue to find break-in targets
item.description: The Vancouver Police Department (VPD) advises residents to inspect their apartment doors for any sign of glue since thieves have used the adhesive to help them break into apartments in the city.

item.title: Pedestrian in serious but stable condition after hit-and-run in Coquitlam
item.description: A pedestrian is in hospital with serious injuries after a hit-and-run in Coquitlam.

item.title: Surrey will host free public watch parties for FIFA matches
item.description: With 100 days to go until the FIFA World Cup arrives in Vancouver, the City of Surrey announced on Tuesday that it will organize live public screenings of the matches this summer.

item.title: Two oppositional councillors table motion to save Vancouver’s Car Free Day festivals
item.description: After the organizer behind Vancouver’s Car Free Days declared it would not proceed with its festivals this year, a pair of councillors have introduced a motion to partially fund the events.
